Operator: Good day, and welcome to the NexusGuard Technologies Q3 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. Instructions for joining the question and answer session will be given at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NexusGuard Technologies' results for Q3 FY2024. With me on today's call are Sarah Kline, Chief Executive Officer; Mike Harlan, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Technology Officer; Tom Reyes, Chief Security Officer; and Jordan Lee, VP of Sales.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Sarah Kline.

Sarah Kline: Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. NexusGuard Technologies continues to demonstrate leadership in the cybersecurity market. We achieved record bookings in Q3, driven by strong demand for our integrated NexusGuard One security platform and our expanding global presence. The positive customer feedback about NexusGuard One and the resulting acceleration in platform adoption and expansions is very encouraging.

We are focused on six strategic priorities: driving down churn through advanced retention strategies, accelerating platform adoption over point products, optimizing channel partner performance, incorporating customer feedback into rapid innovation, maintaining disciplined assumptions in our guidance, and fueling expansion within our existing large accounts.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Harlan to provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

Mike Harlan: Thank you, Sarah. We delivered another quarter of strong financial results. Total revenue for Q3 FY2024 was $385 million, representing a 29% increase year-over-year. We saw significant growth in our subscription revenue, which now accounts for 93% of our total revenue. Gross margin was 82%, while operating expenses were $280 million. Net income was $75 million, resulting in earnings per share of $0.85. We are reiterating our full-year guidance and remain confident in our ability to achieve our financial objectives.

Today, I'd like to dive deeper into our customer churn metrics, which continue to underscore the stickiness of our platform in this high-stakes cybersecurity landscape. For Q3 FY2024, our net revenue retention, or NRR, stood at an impressive 118%, reflecting not just low churn but robust expansion within our existing customer base—particularly from upsells in our XDR and SASE modules amid surging ransomware and supply chain attack vectors like those seen in the Change Healthcare breach earlier this year.

Let's break it down. Our gross dollar churn rate—measuring lost ARR from downgrades and cancellations—was 4.2% annualized, down 90 basis points year-over-year and well below the industry benchmark of 7-9% for enterprise cybersecurity SaaS, as reported in recent Gartner Magic Quadrant analyses. This equates to just 1.05% quarterly churn, with logo churn, or lost customers, at 3.8%, primarily from our mid-market segment where contract values average $250K ARR versus $2.5M in enterprise.

Key drivers of churn, based on our post-churn NPS surveys and customer success data, break out as follows: Budget reallocations and M&A activity accounted for 45% of churned ARR, with economic headwinds persisting and 22% of churn tied to outright budget cuts amid broader IT spend scrutiny. However, M&A was the bigger culprit here—up 15% quarter-over-quarter—as we saw customers like those in the financial services vertical consolidate post-acquisitions, mirroring the consolidation waves following the Okta-Auth0 merger playbook. We've lost pockets of ARR to streamlined stacks, but our multi-tenant architecture has enabled seamless migrations in 70% of these cases.

Competitive displacement made up 28% of churned ARR, with direct competition intensifying from CrowdStrike's Falcon platform and Palo Alto's Cortex XDR siphoning some EDR-focused renewals. Notably, 12% of mid-market churn stemmed from Zscaler's Zero Trust edge in SASE, where customers prioritized bandwidth optimization over our integrated UEBA features. False positive fatigue in threat detection was a sub-factor, affecting 8% of cases, though our ML-tuned Sigma ruleset reduced this by 35% year-over-year.

Technical and integration friction represented 18% of churned ARR, with legacy on-prem holdouts—about 15% of our base—struggling with hybrid cloud migrations to AWS Outposts or Azure Arc. Integration delays with SIEM tools like Splunk or Elastic contributed here, exacerbated by skills gaps in SecOps teams post-layoffs at firms like Cisco.

Other factors accounted for 9%, including regulatory shifts such as EU NIS2 compliance driving some EMEA customers to local providers like Darktrace, and isolated product gaps in OT security for ICS environments.

Regional nuances add color: In North America, which is 72% of ARR, churn was a pristine 3.5%, buoyed by hyperscaler partnerships—our AWS Marketplace velocity is up 40%—and sticky federal contracts under CMMC 2.0. EMEA, at 18% of ARR, ticked up to 6.1% due to GDPR fines pressuring SMBs and DORA prep favoring bundled offerings from Sophos. APAC, 10% of ARR, held at 4.8%, but we saw upticks in Japan from post-Log4Shell remediation fatigue.

Strategic initiatives driving churn compression include our AI-Powered Retention Engine, rolled out in Q2. This predictive churn model—leveraging graph neural networks on telemetry from 500K+ endpoints—flags at-risk accounts 45 days early, with 85% precision. This has rescued $12M ARR year-to-date via proactive playbooks, including auto-tuned EDR policies that cut alert fatigue by 52%.

Customer Success 2.0 has expanded our CSAT teams by 25% to 150 reps, focusing on quarterly business reviews with ROI dashboards benchmarking against MITRE ATT&CK coverage. We've achieved 92% renewal intent in Q3 cohorts.

Product-led retention has deepened integrations with ServiceNow for SOAR workflows and Snowflake for threat intel lakes, reducing switch costs. Our Cyber Resilience Score—a proprietary KPI blending MTTR, coverage gaps, and compliance posture—has become a boardroom staple, driving 22% NRR uplift in engaged accounts.

Economic moat via bundling includes our SecureStack Elite bundles combining CNAPP, CSPM, and CWPP, capturing 65% of expansions and offsetting churn with 2.3x multipliers.

Looking forward, we guide to full-year gross churn below 4.5%, with NRR expanding to 120%+ in FY2025 as our GenAI copilot for threat hunting—already in beta with 50 early adopters—further entrenches us. In a world where dwell times average 21 days per Mandiant M-Trends, customers can't afford churn risks. Our flywheel is accelerating, and we're positioned to outpace peers like SentinelOne and Wiz in retention leadership.

Shifting gears to one of our most critical growth drivers: the accelerating shift from point products to our integrated NexusGuard One platform. This isn't just a buzzword—it's a structural change in the cybersecurity landscape, backed by hard data from our results, customer behavior, and industry benchmarks.

In Q3, platform adoption—defined as customers deploying our full NexusGuard One suite, encompassing EDR, NDR, CWPP, and SASE capabilities on a single agent and console—reached 62% of new ACV bookings. That's up from 48% in Q3 2023 and a 15-point sequential increase from Q2. Conversely, point product sales—standalone modules like our legacy endpoint protection or discrete firewall-as-a-service—dropped to just 22% of new bookings, down from 37% a year ago. The remaining 16% were hybrid expansions, where point users upsell into the platform.

This mix shift directly fueled our results: platform deals carried an average ACV of $1.2 million, 2.7x higher than point products at $445,000. Our dollar-based net expansion rate hit 128% for platform customers versus a stagnant 105% for point-only accounts. Overall ARR from platform customers now stands at $2.8 billion, representing 71% of total ARR—up 1,200 basis points year-over-year. For context, Gartner forecasts that by 2025, 70% of enterprises will consolidate to 3-5 integrated platforms from 20+ point solutions today, and we're riding that wave ahead of the curve.

Customers are tired of the point product proliferation trap. Legacy setups from vendors like Symantec or McAfee often result in 15-20 disparate tools, leading to alert fatigue, integration silos, and 40% higher operational costs per IDC studies. Our platform delivers a true single pane of glass with AI-powered XDR orchestration—real-time correlation across endpoint, network, cloud, and identity signals via our proprietary HyperThreat Engine. In Q3, we launched GenAI Threat Fusion, which automates 85% of triage workflows, reducing MTTR from hours to minutes. Early adopters like a Fortune 50 financial services firm saw a 35% drop in false positives and 28% TCO savings in year one.

Regionally, North America, our bread-and-butter at 55% of revenue, drove 68% platform adoption, fueled by hyperscalers like AWS and Azure pushing Zero Trust mandates. A key win was a $45 million multi-year deal with a Big Four bank, displacing Check Point point firewalls and SentinelOne endpoints in favor of our unified stack. EMEA surged to 58% adoption, up from 42% year-over-year, as GDPR enforcement and NIS2 directives force consolidation—we signed 120 new enterprise logos there, including a European auto OEM migrating from Palo Alto Prisma point modules. APAC lagged at 49%, weighed by data sovereignty hurdles in China and Japan, but our Tokyo data center launch and partnerships with NTT and SoftBank are closing the gap; Q4 pipelines show 20% month-over-month growth.

Strategically, we're doubling down on platformization. We've invested $250 million in FY24 R&D for seamless brownfield migrations—our AutoConsolidate tool now integrates with 95% of incumbent tools like Microsoft Defender or CrowdStrike Falcon via open APIs, achieving 90% success rates in pilots. For SMBs, our Platform Express tier at $50/user/month is converting 40% of point trials, with churn under 5%. Looking ahead, we expect platform adoption to hit 70% of bookings in FY24, driving 25-30% ARR growth and expanding gross margins to 82% as scale efficiencies kick in—platforms have 15-point higher margins due to shared infrastructure.

This shift isn't hype; it's existential for the industry. Point products are commoditizing—witness the 15% year-over-year decline in standalone EPP market share per ESG research—while platforms like ours, Zscaler's Zero Trust Exchange, or Palo Alto's Strata enable outcome-based selling: not buy a firewall, but stop breaches with 99.9% efficacy. We're positioned as leaders in the $85 billion platform market growing at 22% CAGR.

Next, I'll turn to our channel partner performance and their critical contribution to revenue, which remains a cornerstone of our go-to-market strategy here at NexusGuard Technologies.

The cybersecurity landscape is more fragmented and complex than ever, with escalating threats like ransomware-as-a-service operations—think LockBit 3.0 evolutions—and supply chain compromises reminiscent of SolarWinds. In this environment, our channel ecosystem of over 4,500 partners worldwide, including value-added resellers, managed service providers, system integrators, and distributors like TD Synnex and Ingram Micro, is indispensable. They don't just sell; they architect, deploy, and manage our portfolio—from our flagship Nexus Endpoint Guardian EDR platform to our Nexus SecureEdge SASE solution and AI-powered Nexus ThreatForge XDR.

Headline numbers for Q3 and FY24 to date: Channel partners drove 68% of our total revenue, up from 62% in FY23, marking our highest contribution ever. This equates to $285 million in Q3 channel bookings alone, a blistering 32% year-over-year growth, outpacing our direct sales growth of 18%. On a full-year basis, channel revenue is tracking to $1.02 billion, representing 28% year-over-year expansion and contributing to our overall ARR of $1.8 billion, with channel-attributable ARR growing 25% to $1.15 billion.

Breaking it down by partner tier, our Platinum partners—top-tier elite like CDW, Insight Enterprises, and Softchoice—accounted for 45% of channel revenue, delivering an average ACV of $1.2 million per deal, up 15% year-over-year. These partners are deeply invested in our Nexus Partner Accelerator Program, where we've certified over 1,200 engineers on our latest Nexus Zero Trust Architecture stack. Gold and Silver tiers, including regional MSPs like Pax8 and Evernex, contributed 35% and 20% respectively, with MSPs showing the fastest ramp: their net revenue retention hit 125%, fueled by sticky managed detection and response services layered on our platform.

A key trend is the shift toward subscription-led growth. Channel deals now average 85% subscription mix, with multi-year commitments pushing TCV to $2.8 million on average for Platinum wins. We've seen a 40% year-over-year surge in partner-led upsells and cross-sells, particularly bundling our Nexus CloudShield CWP with SecureEdge SASE—a response to the 300% rise in cloud misconfigurations reported by Gartner post-Log4Shell.

Regionally, performance was robust. In the Americas, 55% of channel revenue at $560 million FY24 pace, we posted 35% year-over-year growth, led by hyperscaler co-sell motions. Partners transacting via AWS Marketplace and Azure Marketplace generated $180 million—double year-over-year—thanks to our SteelConnect integrations and FedRAMP High authorization, which unlocked massive public sector deals with VARs like Carahsoft. Ransomware fatigue in healthcare and financial services drove this, with deals like our $15 million TCV win with a top-5 U.S. bank via CDW.

EMEA, at 28% of channel mix or $285 million, grew 22% year-over-year despite macro headwinds like the UK recession. DACH and France shone: 42% growth in Germany on NIS2 compliance tailwinds, where SIs like Bechtle deployed Nexus ThreatForge for 50+ enterprise SOC modernizations. UK partners like Computacenter emphasized our GenAI threat detection modules, countering the 60% uptick in AI-exploited phishing per our Q3 Threat Report.

APAC, our growth engine at 17% of channel revenue or $175 million, exploded 48% year-over-year, propelled by Singapore and Japan mandates like the Cybersecurity Act amendments. Distributors like SHI International Japan facilitated $40 million in bookings, with MSPs focusing on OT security for manufacturing—our Nexus ICS Protect solution saw 3x adoption amid rising state-sponsored attacks targeting critical infrastructure.

Strategically, we've doubled down on partner enablement. Our revamped Partner Portal features AI-driven deal registration scoring, predicting close rates with 92% accuracy using proprietary ML models trained on 10,000+ historical deals. We've invested $25 million in FY24 for virtual bootcamps, certifying 2,500 partners on Nexus 6.0—our platform update with behavioral AI for zero-day evasion, integrated with MITRE ATT&CK frameworks. This yielded a 3x ROI: partner-sourced pipeline grew 55% to $2.4 billion.

We're pioneering partner-first innovations like our Nexus Co-Sell Engine, a Salesforce-integrated tool that auto-generates joint proposals with hyperscalers, slashing sales cycles by 40%. In response to market consolidation—Palo Alto's acquisition spree and CrowdStrike's Falcon expansions—we're prioritizing platformization, where partners build custom Nexus apps via our low-code SDK, fostering lock-in. Early wins include a VAR developing a healthcare-specific HIPAA compliance module atop ThreatForge.

Looking forward, we expect channel to hit 70% of revenue in FY25, with 25-30% growth guided on $1.3 billion. Risks like elongated sales cycles from economic uncertainty are mitigated by our 118% NRR overall and partner-led consumption models. We're excited about Q4 ramps in sovereign cloud deals—India's PDPB compliance wave—and deeper MSSP integrations for autonomous SOCs.

In summary, our channel ecosystem isn't just performing; it's transforming how enterprises operationalize cybersecurity in a post-quantum, AI-threat world.

I'd also like to highlight customer feedback on our new products and features, one of our most critical leading indicators. In the cybersecurity landscape—where threats evolve faster than Moore's Law, with ransomware attacks up 37% year-over-year per Chainalysis data and nation-state actors like APT41 ramping up supply chain exploits—customer validation is our North Star for product innovation and market leadership.

Our Net Promoter Score for new releases hit 78 in Q3, up from 62 a year ago and our highest quarterly score ever. This is driven by direct feedback from over 4,200 enterprise customers surveyed through our Voice of the Customer program, including Fortune 500 names like a major U.S. bank and a European telco giant. Churn among new feature adopters dropped to sub-2%, compared to the industry average of 8-10% for SaaS security tools per Gartner. Upsell attach rates for our latest innovations reached 42%, contributing $18 million in net new ARR—about 15% of our total Q3 bookings.

Drilling into specifics: Our Nexus XDR Platform's GenAI-Powered Anomaly Detection module, launched in Q1, has customers raving about the 65% reduction in mean time to response, now averaging 14 minutes versus 40 pre-launch—echoing CrowdStrike's Falcon XDR gains but with our proprietary federated learning model that preserves data sovereignty for GDPR-heavy regions. False positive rates plummeted 55% to under 3%, alleviating alert fatigue in SOC teams. A tier-1 healthcare provider shared that it freed up 30% of analyst time for proactive threat hunting. Adoption stands at 87% among our top 500 customers, with 92% renewal intent. We're iterating on natural language query enhancements based on requests from 68% of beta users.

The Secure Access Service Edge Fabric 2.0, with integrated Zero Trust Network Access and Cloud Workload Protection, has been a game-changer amid the 50% surge in cloud-native attacks per Mandiant's M-Trends. NPS here is 82, fueled by 40% faster deployment times—down to 2 weeks from 5—thanks to agentless onboarding via eBPF kernel tech. North America leads with 91% adoption among our 1,200 commercial accounts, but APAC exploded 28% quarter-over-quarter to 62% penetration, driven by Singapore's PDPA updates and Japan's My Number Act mandates mirroring U.S. CMMC 2.0. EMEA feedback highlights our SWG/DLP convergence, with a UK financial services firm noting 75% fewer data exfiltration attempts post-deployment. This positions us to capture share from Zscaler and Palo Alto's Prisma, where our pricing at $28 per user/month undercuts them by 15-20% while delivering 2.5x better throughput.

On the endpoint side, FalconEdge EDR's Ransomware Shield feature scores 79 NPS post-SolarWinds and Log4Shell echoes, with customers demanding behavioral analytics over signature-based detection. 76% of users reported zero successful encryptions in simulated red-team exercises—benchmarking against Microsoft Defender's 68% efficacy in MITRE ATT&CK evals. We've seen a 35% year-over-year increase in multi-product bundle uptake. A mid-market retailer in LATAM cited 50% cost savings on incident response, crediting our auto-remediation playbooks.

Emerging features like our Quantum-Resistant Encryption toolkit have early adopter feedback from 150 beta customers in defense and finance—85% plan full rollout by year-end—praising compatibility with post-quantum algorithms like Kyber and Dilithium, ahead of NIST's 2024 standardization. This addresses the Harvest Now, Decrypt Later threat from quantum adversaries.

Regionally, North America is 72% of feedback volume, EMEA grew 22% quarter-over-quarter on NIS2 tailwinds, APAC/Japan hit 19% share with 95% satisfaction on localized threat intel feeds covering Lazarus Group. LATAM underscores affordability, with 80% citing our pay-as-you-grow model amid currency volatility.

This feedback is reshaping our roadmap. We're doubling down on AI-orchestrated XDR with $50 million in R&D for FY25, targeting 90% MTTR sub-10 minutes. Partnerships with AWS and ServiceNow integrate natively, addressing 62% of requests. 88% of Q2 detractors converted to promoters post-support, proof our 118% NRR isn't luck.

Before moving on, let me turn to our performance in expansion within existing large accounts, a cornerstone of our land-and-expand strategy. We define large accounts as those generating over $1 million in ARR, our top 20% of customers by spend. These enterprise clients—primarily Fortune 1000 in financial services, healthcare, critical infrastructure, and tech—now account for 68% of our total ARR, up from 62% a year ago.

Our dollar-based NRR for these large accounts reached 128% in Q3, the ninth consecutive quarter above 120% and accelerating from 118% last year. This translates to $245 million in expansion revenue from this cohort alone, a 32% year-over-year increase. 85% came from net upsells and cross-sells—adding new modules to SecureX unified platform—while 15% from seat expansions tied to headcount and hybrid workforces. Churn remained under 1%, underscoring stickiness.

Key initiatives: Our AI-powered XDR has large accounts initially landing with NGFW and EDR rapidly expanding for correlated threat hunting across endpoints, networks, cloud, and identity. 47 large accounts adopted XDR in Q3, driving 42% average ACV uplift or $450,000 per account, resonant amid ransomware-as-a-service with 25% rise in living-off-the-land techniques per MITRE ATT&CK that our XDR neutralizes.

ZTNA and SASE bundles accelerated expansions in cloud-heavy environments. Large accounts integrating with AWS and Azure alongside Splunk or Elastic consolidate by layering SASE. A major U.S. bank expanded from $2.8 million ARR in NGFW to $5.1 million adding SASE and CWPP for Kubernetes against container escapes like Log4Shell exploits. Over 120 SASE POCs converted 92% to paid expansions within 90 days.

North America contributed 72% of expansion dollars with 135% NRR, buoyed by SEC cyber rules and National Cybersecurity Strategy. EMEA at 145% NRR driven by NIS2 deadlines; 18 DAX 40 firms averaged 55% ACV growth with SOAR integrations to ServiceNow and Cortex XSOAR. APAC at 112% NRR trending up 18 points, fueled by PDPA and Australia's Act—three top-5 Japanese banks expanded to CASB for shadow IT.

This validates our platform approach as Gartner projects $215 billion spend in 2025, 45% growth in MDR. Customer success teams target 15-20% wallet share via QBRs. RPO from large accounts grew 41% to $4.2 billion, 78% within 12 months.

We expect large account NRR at 125-130% through FY25, supported by 4.2-year contracts and GenAI feeds reducing MTTD 60%. This outpaces Zscaler's 115-120% via 98% gross retention and vertical playbooks.

Finally, before we open for questions, the key assumptions underpinning our FY25 guidance, announced this morning: total revenue $1.45 billion to $1.48 billion, 28% to 31% growth at midpoint; ARR ending $1.32 billion to $1.35 billion, up 30%; non-GAAP operating margins 22% to 24%; adjusted free cash flow $420 million to $440 million. These reflect confidence in our leadership per Gartner and Forrester.

Core pillars: Demand assumes 95%+ dollar retention, 125% DBNER, subscription 85% of growth. 450-500 net new logos at $650K ACV, 98% gross retention, 35-38% RPO growth.

Product/GTM: GA NexusGuard Fabric Q1 FY25 for SASE share, 65% pilot conversion; ML analytics reduce false positives 25%, 30% MDR growth. Channel 22% growth, marketplaces 35% new ARR; sales 1.2x quota.

Macro/regional: Recession-resistant 13.5% spend growth per Gartner amid 28% nation-state attacks. Americas 58%, EMEA 26%, APAC 16%; 5% USD headwind, 2% APAC geo drag.

Costs: Gross 82-83% with GPU efficiencies; OpEx 59% via leverage; SBC $180M; FCF 95%+ conversion.

Risks: 5% DBNER shortfall shaves 3 points growth; AI attach unlocks high end. Supply chain mitigated, regs 10% uplift.

Grounded in $2.1 billion pipeline up 32%.

Lisa Patel: Thank you, Mike. Our engineering team is laser-focused on innovation and delivering cutting-edge security solutions. We are leveraging artificial intelligence and machine learning to enhance our threat detection and response capabilities. Key areas of focus include advancing our GenAI Threat Fusion and quantum-resistant encryption toolkit, as highlighted in customer feedback, while pushing platform integrations for seamless XDR across hybrid environments.

Tom Reyes: Security remains our top priority. We are constantly monitoring the threat landscape—from ransomware evolutions to nation-state supply chain exploits—and adapting our security posture to protect our customers and our own infrastructure, with a sharp eye on compliance like NIS2 and CMMC.

Jordan Lee: Thank you. We are seeing strong demand for our solutions across all geographies and industry verticals. Our sales team is executing well, expanding channel partnerships to reach a wider audience, as Mike detailed, with robust pipeline growth in APAC and EMEA.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator: Thank you. Instructions for the Q&A session: Please press star then 1 on your touchtone phone now if you would like to ask a question. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith: Thanks, and congrats on the strong quarter. Sarah, can you talk about competitive dynamics, especially with CrowdStrike and Palo Alto pushing aggressively on platforms?

Sarah Kline: Thanks, John. We're seeing the market consolidate toward integrated platforms, as Mike outlined with our 62% adoption rate. Our HyperThreat Engine and GenAI capabilities give us an edge in reducing MTTR and false positives, winning displacements like the Big Four bank deal. Customers value our single-pane outcomes over point sprawl, positioning us strongly against those incumbents.

Operator: Next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Emily Chen: Great, thanks. Mike, on the FY25 guidance, could you elaborate more on the macro sensitivities and how you're thinking about IT budget scrutiny?

Mike Harlan: Absolutely, Emily. As I noted, we're modeling cybersecurity as recession-resistant with 13.5% global growth per Gartner, prioritizing amid rising threats. We bake in conservative new logo ramps and a 5% USD headwind, with mitigants like 125%+ DBNER from expansions. A 5% shortfall in retention would trim growth by 3 points, but our $2.1 billion pipeline and RPO visibility give us conviction.

Operator: Next question comes from Raj Patel with Barclays.

Raj Patel: Thanks. Lisa, what's the roadmap look like for AI integrations and how they tie into SASE expansions?

Lisa Patel: Good question, Raj. Building on Q3 launches, we're allocating $50 million in FY25 R&D to hit sub-10 minute MTTR with AI-orchestrated XDR. NexusGuard Fabric GA in Q1 will unify SASE/SWG/CASB with hyperscalers, converting 65% of pilots. Federated learning ensures sovereignty, as seen in 87% adoption of our anomaly detection among top customers.

Operator: Next question comes from Lisa Wong with JPMorgan.

Lisa Wong: Hi, thanks. Tom, with all the regulatory shifts like NIS2 and SEC rules, how are you seeing that impact threat monitoring and customer security postures?

Tom Reyes: Thanks, Lisa. Regulations are tailwinds, driving 145% NRR in EMEA large accounts and federal wins via FedRAMP. We're adapting with localized intel feeds, like for Lazarus in APAC, and SOAR integrations that cut dwell times. Our Cyber Resilience Score helps boards quantify posture, fueling renewals and expansions.

Sarah Kline: Thank you for your thoughtful questions. We believe we are well-positioned to capitalize on the growing demand for cybersecurity solutions. Thank you to our employees, customers, and partners for their continued support.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our call. You may now disconnect.
